questions.stem: Tehri Dam, the tallest dam in India, is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Tehri Dam (Uttarakhand): 260.5 m high — tallest in India and one of the world's tallest. Built on the Bhagirathi river. Multipurpose: power (1000 MW), irrigation, and drinking water.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Bhakra Nangal Dam is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Bhakra Dam (Himachal Pradesh, on Sutlej) + Nangal Barrage (Punjab) = Bhakra-Nangal Project. Nehru called it a 'temple of modern India'. 225.5 m high.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Sardar Sarovar Dam (Gujarat, on Narmada): 138.7 m. Benefits: irrigation (Gujarat, Maharashtra, Rajasthan, MP) and power. The Narmada Bachao Andolan opposed displacement of tribals.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Hirakud Dam, the longest dam in India (~4.8 km), is on which river?
questions.explanation: Hirakud Dam (Odisha): on the Mahanadi river. Completed 1957 — one of India's first major multipurpose river projects after independence.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Nagarjuna Sagar Dam is built on which river?
questions.explanation: Nagarjuna Sagar (Telangana/Andhra Pradesh boundary on Krishna): completed 1967. Named after Buddhist monk Nagarjuna who built a university here. 124 m high, masonry dam.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Tungabhadra Dam is a joint project of which two states?
questions.explanation: Tungabhadra Dam (Hospet, Karnataka): joint project of Andhra Pradesh and Karnataka on the Tungabhadra river. Irrigates Raichur and Bellary districts.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Mettur Dam (Stanley Reservoir) is in which state?
questions.explanation: Mettur Dam (Salem district, Tamil Nadu): on the Cauvery river. Completed 1934 — one of India's oldest dams. Opening Mettur Dam gates signals the traditional farming season in the Cauvery Delta.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Farakka Barrage was built to:

options.option_text: Divert Ganga water to flush the Hooghly river and maintain Kolkata port

questions.explanation: Farakka Barrage (West Bengal): diverts Ganga water through a feeder canal to the Hooghly to maintain navigability of Kolkata port. Has been a long-standing dispute between India and Bangladesh.
questions.subject: Geography

questions.stem: The Krishnarajasagar (KRS) Dam, a major irrigation reservoir near Mysuru, is constructed across which river?

options.option_text: Kabini River, a tributary of Cauvery in Karnataka
Cauvery River, near Krishnarajasagara in Mysuru district
Hemavati River, a tributary of Cauvery in Karnataka
Shimsha River, originating in the Karnataka plateau

questions.explanation: The KRS Dam is built across the Cauvery River at Krishnarajasagara, about 12 km from Mysuru. Kabini and Hemavati are tributaries of the Cauvery but their dams are at different locations — Kabini Dam is at Beechanahalli and Hemavati Dam is at Gorur — both are common confusions for this question.

questions.stem: The Ukai Dam (Vallabhsagar Reservoir), the largest dam in Gujarat, is built across which river?

options.option_text: Sabarmati River, flowing through Ahmedabad city
Mahi River, draining the central Gujarat region
Tapi River, flowing westward into the Gulf of Khambhat
Narmada River, regulated by the Sardar Sarovar Dam

questions.explanation: Ukai Dam is built on the Tapi (Tapti) River in Tapi district, Gujarat. Sardar Sarovar Dam — the more famous Gujarat dam — is on the Narmada, making it a strong distractor. Mahi Dam at Kadana is another Gujarat dam, but on the Mahi river, not Tapi.

questions.stem: The Rihand Dam, which creates India's largest artificial lake known as Govind Ballabh Pant Sagar, is located in which state?

options.option_text: Madhya Pradesh, in Rewa district near the Vindhya range
Uttar Pradesh, in Sonbhadra district near the MP border
Jharkhand, in the southern Chotanagpur Plateau region
Chhattisgarh, in Surguja district on the Rihand river

questions.explanation: Rihand Dam is in Sonbhadra district, Uttar Pradesh; the reservoir extends into MP but the dam structure is in UP. Madhya Pradesh is the most common wrong answer because the Rihand River originates in MP and the reservoir backwaters spread into MP's Singrauli district. Chhattisgarh is plausible since the Rihand river's upper catchment lies there.

questions.stem: The Almatti Dam on the Krishna River became the centre of a prolonged inter-state water dispute between Karnataka and which other state, primarily over reduced downstream flows?

options.option_text: Maharashtra, over Krishna waters in Sangli district
Telangana, over submergence of Nagarjuna Sagar backwaters
Andhra Pradesh, over depleted inflows to the Krishna delta
Goa, over Mahadayi-Krishna inter-basin diversion plans

questions.explanation: Andhra Pradesh (before bifurcation) protested Karnataka's plan to raise the Almatti Dam's height, arguing it would reduce Krishna inflows to the AP delta and harm Nagarjuna Sagar storage. Telangana is a tempting answer because it now inherits parts of Krishna basin, but Andhra Pradesh was the original claimant before the 2014 bifurcation. The dispute went to the KWDT.

questions.stem: The Dul Hasti Hydroelectric Project, commissioned in phases in the Kishtwar region, harnesses which river in Jammu & Kashmir?

options.option_text: Jhelum River, flowing through the Srinagar valley
Ravi River, originating near Bara Bhangal in Himachal Pradesh
Chenab River, one of the five rivers of the Punjab system
Beas River, flowing through the Kullu Valley in Himachal Pradesh

questions.explanation: Dul Hasti HEP (390 MW) is built on the Chenab River in Kishtwar district, J&K. The Salal and Baglihar dams on the Chenab are better-known, making Dul Hasti a niche PYQ pick. Jhelum is wrong because it flows through Srinagar, not Kishtwar. Ravi and Beas projects are in Himachal Pradesh.

questions.stem: The Tehri Dam reservoir permanently submerged old Tehri town along with the natural confluence of the Bhagirathi River and which other river at that site?

options.option_text: Alaknanda River, whose confluence at Devprayag is downstream
Mandakini River, descending from the Kedarnath glacier area
Bhilangana River, which joined Bhagirathi at old Tehri town
Tons River, the largest Yamuna tributary in Uttarakhand

questions.explanation: The Bhilangana River, originating near Khatling glacier, joined the Bhagirathi at old Tehri — this precise confluence was submerged by the reservoir. Alaknanda is the most tempting distractor because it merges with Bhagirathi to form the Ganga at Devprayag, but Devprayag is downstream and not submerged. Mandakini joins the Alaknanda at Rudraprayag, unrelated to Tehri.

questions.stem: The Polavaram Multipurpose Project on the Godavari, declared a National Project in 2014, routes water through its Right Main Canal primarily to benefit which river basin's irrigation network?

options.option_text: Penna River basin in the Rayalaseema region of Andhra Pradesh
Krishna River basin via the Eluru–Bandar link canal system
Vamsadhara River basin along the Odisha–Andhra Pradesh border
Nagavali River basin in the Srikakulam–Vizianagaram region

questions.explanation: Polavaram's Right Main Canal (RMC, ~174 km) carries Godavari surplus water westward, linking it to the Krishna delta via the Eluru Canal and terminating near Bandar (Machilipatnam, Krishna district). This inter-basin transfer from Godavari to Krishna basin is the key engineering purpose of the RMC. Vamsadhara and Nagavali are served by the Left Bank irrigation of Polavaram, not the RMC, making them plausible distractors.
